title: Soft-reserve indexed KV pools with stochastic compaction playbook
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem statement:
We observe increasing tail latency and out-of-memory (OOM) incidents on 80B model shards under bursty traffic with heterogeneous sequence lengths. Root cause analysis points to persistent internal fragmentation of the KV cache: many small uncoalesced free segments and long-lived pinned entries (long sequences or stuck sessions). This reduces effective cache capacity, and combined with continuous batching, causes sudden batch-size regressions and evictions.

Goal:
Design and implement a low-risk allocation and background compaction strategy that: 1) reduces fragmentation without high CPU/GPU overhead, 2) is compatible with continuous batching and per-request latency SLOs, 3) preserves cache hit-rate for short-lived sessions, and 4) provides telemetry to detect and rollback if regressions occur.

Proposed approach (high level):
1) Indexed soft-reservation pools: maintain multiple size-class pools (tiny, small, medium, large) with light-weight per-GPU bitmaps and a soft-reserve quota for each tenant/worker. Soft-reserve means an allocation can succeed even if the pool is temporarily above quota but will be penalized for evictions when under pressure. This prevents global pool starvation while avoiding hard failures.

2) Stochastic async compaction: instead of heavy stop-the-world compaction, run probabilistic background compaction workers that pick candidate GPU memory slabs based on a fragmentation score (free-run-length distribution + pinned ratio) and attempt small relocations when GPU utilization < 40% or within scheduled maintenance windows. Relocations are done with opportunistic KV entry copy, pointer swap, and free list update; each relocation is bounded in tokens/time to avoid impacting inference.

3) Sequence-length aware watermarks: keep short-term histogram of sequence-lengths per route and bias allocation towards size-classes matching the dominant seq lengths. This reduces cross-size churn and the creation of undersized holes.

4) Eviction priority with recency vs. reuse score: integrate reuse telemetry (KV touch frequency and predicted future reuse from recent request context) into eviction scoring, so soft-reserve entries with low reuse are preferred for compaction/eviction.

5) Compact-on-allocate fallback: if an allocation fails and free capacity exists fragmented across many small slots, trigger an immediate bounded compaction attempt targeted to reclaim one contiguous slot large enough for the request. This is limited to a short budget (e.g., 1ms or N relocations) to preserve tail latency.

Telemetry & observability:
- Fragmentation heatmap per GPU (occupied run lengths, free-run-length distribution) and trendlines.
- Pool occupancy vs. effective usable capacity (after fragmentation) metric.
- Compaction activity traces (start/end, relocated entries, time taken, batch impact).
- Eviction reasons histogram (pressure, soft-reserve overflow, pinned eviction, manual).
- Per-route cache hit-rate and sequence-length histogram (to tune size-classes).

Benchmarks and safety checks:
- Microbench: synthetic workloads with mixed seq length (8/64/1024) and burst patterns to measure compaction overhead and hit-rate delta.
- End-to-end: replay production traces (sanitized) to ensure tail latency < SLO and OOMs reduced.
- Canary rollout: Gradual enablement by model shard and region with ability to rollback via runtime flag.

Trade-offs and rationale:
- Why soft-reserve? Hard tenant reservations can under-utilize memory and are brittle under workload shifts. Soft-reserves provide a fairness signal without causing hard failures; eviction policies enforce them when needed.
- Why stochastic compaction instead of periodic global compaction? Global compaction risks large pauses and GPU contention. Stochastic, bounded relocations reduce worst-case interference and can adapt to utilization.
- Cost: We accept modest extra GPU memory copies and a small increase in background GPU utilization in exchange for higher usable cache capacity and fewer OOMs.

Implementation plan (phases):
Phase 1 (design & infra hooks, 2 weeks):
- Define size classes and soft-reserve accounting model.
- Add telemetry counters and heatmap proto.
- Add runtime flags and feature gate for canary.

Phase 2 (soft-reserve allocator, 3 weeks):
- Implement indexed pools with per-GPU metadata and allocation fallbacks.
- Implement eviction scorer integration with reuse telemetry.
- Unit tests and local perf microbench.

Phase 3 (stochastic compaction, 3 weeks):
- Background worker that samples slabs with fragmentation score, performs bounded relocations and updates pointers atomically.
- Implement compact-on-allocate short-path.
- Add safety checks: relocation limit per-second per-GPU, compaction cooldown windows.

Phase 4 (canary & rollout, 2 weeks):
- Canary deploy to low-traffic shards, run production replay, monitor telemetry dashboards.
- Iterate thresholds (soft-reserve ratios, relocation budgets).

Rollout/QA checklist:
- Unit tests for allocator invariants and pointer swaps.
- Regression tests for latency with synthetic continuous batching scenarios.
- Dashboard + alert: sudden spike in compaction activity or increase in p99 latency triggers auto-disable.
- Github PRs: link to PR-? (TBD) and design doc in Confluence.

Open questions / risks:
- Interaction with multi-GPU sharding and cross-GPU KV references: ensure relocations don't break cross-GPU pointers.
- Worst-case overhead when many kernels schedule compaction concurrently across GPUs. Mitigate via global compaction token bucket.
- Accuracy of reuse predictor for eviction ordering; may need a fallback LRU bias.

Expected outcomes:
- 10-25% increase in effective KV cache capacity under mixed workloads (measured as usable contiguous bytes).
- Reduction in OOM incidents for large models by >50% in worst-affected clusters.
- Small CPU/GPU overhead from background relocations; tuned to be invisible within latency SLOs.

- Perf harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/kv-perf/tree/soft-reserve
